code: unsigned char *desc = blkid_probe_get_buffer(pr, off, max(sizeof(struct boot_record), sizeof(struct iso_volume_descriptor)));
note: Raw attacker-controlled file bytes are read at sector offsets starting at 0x8000; the descriptor type byte desc[0] selects the PVD (0x01) and the supplementary/Joliet descriptor (0x02).
Supplementary descriptor accepted as Joliet when escape_sequences matches "%/@"; the 128-byte joliet->volume_set_id field is fully attacker-controlled UTF-16BE data.
merge_utf16be_ascii() is called with 128-byte volume_set_id fields and writes into the 256-byte stack buffer buf[] of probe_iso9660 (no size check precedes this call).

Root cause: loop termination depends only on the ASCII index a and UTF-16 index u, never on the output index o. Each surrogate pair (utf16[u] in 0xD8..0xDB with utf16[u+2] in 0xDC..0xDF) advances o by 4 while a advances by only 1, so 32 surrogate pairs over the 128-byte input reach o=128 with only 32 of 128 ASCII characters consumed; the trailing ASCII loop then grows the total output to 2*128 + 2*32 = 320 bytes.
Sink: out-of-bounds write past the end of the 256-byte buf[] caller buffer; o reaches 320, writing 64 bytes beyond the buffer (stack-buffer-overflow).
